sentiment.rationale: Dell raised its full-year AI server shipment guidance from roughly $20 billion to roughly $25 billion, and raised full-year revenue guidance to $111.7 billion at the midpoint, up 17% year over year, with Q4 revenue guidance of $31.5 billion at the midpoint, up 32%. Management expressed high confidence in AI momentum, citing record orders of $12.3 billion in Q3 and a record backlog of $18.4 billion. However, the company acknowledged significant commodity cost pressures (DRAM, NAND, hard drives) that could impact margins, and management's recovery expectations, while optimistic, are not guaranteed, tempering the score slightly.

summary.revenue: Record third-quarter revenue of $27.0 billion, up 11% year over year. Full-year FY26 revenue expected between $111.2 billion and $112.2 billion, up 17% at the midpoint of $111.7 billion. Q4 FY26 revenue expected between $31.0 billion and $32.0 billion, up 32% at the midpoint of $31.5 billion.
summary.eps: Diluted EPS of $2.28, up 39% year over year; record third-quarter non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.59, up 17%. Full-year FY26 GAAP diluted EPS expected to be $8.38 at the midpoint, up 31%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS to be $9.92 at the midpoint, up 22%. Q4 FY26 GAAP diluted EPS expected to be $3.05 at the midpoint, up 42%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS to be $3.50 at the midpoint, up 31%.
summary.guidance: Full-year FY26 revenue expected between $111.2 billion and $112.2 billion, up 17% at the midpoint of $111.7 billion. Full-year AI server shipments expected to be roughly $25 billion, up over 150%. Full-year FY26 GAAP diluted EPS expected to be $8.38 at the midpoint, up 31%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS to be $9.92 at the midpoint, up 22%. Q4 FY26 revenue expected between $31.0 billion and $32.0 billion, up 32% at the midpoint of $31.5 billion. Q4 FY26 GAAP diluted EPS expected to be $3.05 at the midpoint, up 42%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS to be $3.50 at the midpoint, up 31%.
summary.margin: Gross margin was up 4% to $5.7 billion, or 21.1% of revenue. Operating income grew 11% to $2.5 billion or 9.3% of revenue. ISG operating income rate was up 360 basis points sequentially to 12.4% of revenue. CSG operating income was $0.7 billion, or 6% of revenue.
key_risks: Commodity cost increases across DRAM, NAND, hard drives, and leading-edge nodes, with demand ahead of supply, potentially impacting margins.
Potential inability to fully recover cost increases through pricing, despite management's confidence in doing better than the normal two-thirds recovery.
Consumer revenue declined 7% year over year, though demand returned to growth.
Storage revenue declined 1% year over year.
Forward-looking statements include risks such as adverse global economic conditions, trade disruptions, competitive pressures, and supply chain dependencies.
key_opportunities: AI momentum accelerating with record orders of $12.3 billion in Q3 and $30 billion year to date, with a record backlog of $18.4 billion and a five-quarter pipeline multiples of backlog.
PC refresh cycle durable, with Windows 11 upgrade opportunity and AI PCs driving demand.
Traditional server demand growing double digits, with data center modernization and consolidation.
Dell IP storage portfolio seeing strong demand, with PowerStore growing for seven consecutive quarters.
Capital return program with $1.6 billion returned in Q3 and $5.3 billion year to date.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management used confident language such as 'AI momentum is accelerating,' 'record Q3 revenue,' and 'we are well-positioned to capitalize on AI infrastructure build-outs,' while also acknowledging commodity headwinds but expressing confidence in mitigation.
